item.title: Imagining Post-growth
item.content:encoded:
Fred Basso, London School of Economics and Political Science

Nil Özçağlar-Toulouse, Université de Lille

Julien Troiville, ESG Université du Québec À Montréal

This special issue addresses the urgent need to rethink marketing's role in a post-growth future. With humanity facing catastrophic climate change caused primarily by human activity, marketing must shift from promoting unlimited consumption to supporting genuinely sustainable lifestyles. Post-growth, increasingly studied across environmental sciences, economics, and social sciences, challenges societies' dependence on economic growth and questions the link between prosperity and consumerism.

The special issue seeks contributions exploring three interconnected questions: how marketing can challenge growth-oriented systems and critique its own pro-growth practices; how marketing can support degrowth transitions and transform economic practices; and how marketing can function within a post-growth economy while meeting human needs within planetary boundaries. Contributions should bridge theory and practice, examining tensions between individual and systemic responsibility, alternative practices, and marketing's evolving role.

Appel publié par Recherche et Applications en Marketing (French Edition). Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How marketing can challenge the status quo and question growth-oriented practices, including the critique of desire creation, ethical marketing practices, and the individualization of consumer responsibility
  • How marketing can engage in degrowth practices and implement transformative strategies, including conceptual clarification of degrowth-related concepts and reinventing marketing practices and education
  • How a post-growth economy can be maintained, including the transition from unlimited desires to meeting human needs within consumption corridors and the role of marketing in supporting sufficient lifestyles
  • Critical examination of marketing's role in climate change and planetary boundaries, questioning the relationship between prosperity, productivism, and economic growth
  • Marketing education and pedagogy in the context of post-growth transitions, including decolonial and indigenous perspectives
  • Empirical and conceptual research addressing post-growth marketing from various theoretical, methodological, and disciplinary angles
  • Research in non-WEIRD contexts and with decolonial and indigenous perspectives

Timeline

  • May 1, 2026: Submission platform opens
  • July 1, 2026: Special issue publication date
  • January 15, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Rethinking Regional Skills: Place-Based Capabilities and Economic Transformation
item.content:encoded:
David Morris, University of Nottingham

Carlo Corradini, University of Reading

Lisa De Propris, University of Birmingham

Duygu Buyukyazici, London School of Economics and Political Science

Skills are central to regional development, influencing labour markets, industrial evolution, and economic trajectories. Yet despite their long-standing recognition, regional skills are often under-theorised and frequently conflated with education, human capital, or occupational structures. Conceptual frameworks that treat skills as multidimensional, place-based capabilities that emerge from the interactions of people, firms, and local institutions remain limited, and systematic empirical evidence on skill formation, mismatch, mobility, and utilisation across regions is still sparse. Meanwhile, rapid skill-biased technological change, digitalisation, and green transitions are reshaping jobs, tasks, and production systems, altering regional skill demands, reinforcing divergence in development paths, and raising urgent policy questions.

Appel publié par Regional Studies. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • The nature and dynamics of regional skills formation and transformation due to technological change (skills creation, resilience, obsolescence, disappearance)
  • The links between education, skills transformation and job dynamics in the green and digital transitions of regional economies
  • The drivers and barriers of a regional skills transition for the innovation, growth and resilience of regional economies
  • The regional skill mismatch and skill formation in new labour spaces, e.g. green jobs, remote working, new platformised digital industries, gig economy
  • The enablers and barriers of a regional skills transformation for the green and digital transitions of industrial clusters and regional economies
  • Regional skills transformation and mismatch within shifting regional labour markets
  • Regional skills transformation and mismatch in regions as open economies: skills mobility, remote skills and migration
  • The opportunities and constraints of stranded and stressed regions: left-behindedness, regional low-skill traps, transitioning carbon-intensive regions
  • The links between vocational education, lifelong training and on-the-job upskilling and regional skills transition in the context of technological change
  • The opportunities and constraints of regional skills transition in emerging and developing economies
  • Policy debates and policy experiences to address the regional dimension of skill mismatch, skill formation and skill transition for just and inclusive growth

Timeline

  • June 12, 2026: Abstract deadline
  • September 25, 2026: Manuscript deadline
